title.zh: 卷一百三十六 僭偽列傳三: 王建 孟知祥
title.en: Volume 136: Biographies of Usurpers 3 - Wang Jian, Meng Zhixiang
title.raw: 卷一百三十六 僭偽列傳三: 王建 孟知祥 Volume 136: Biographies of Usurpers 3 - Wang Jian, Meng Zhixiang

sentences.zh: 王建，陳州項城人。

translations.literal: Wang Jian was a native of Xiangcheng in Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian came from Xiangcheng in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐末，隸名於忠武軍。

translations.literal: In the late Tang, his name was enrolled in the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Tang, he was listed on the rolls of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權據蔡州，懸重賞以募之，建始自行間得補軍候。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan held Cai Prefecture and offered rich rewards to recruit men; Jian first obtained appointment as a military scout by going among them on his own.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Zongquan held Cai Prefecture and posted heavy bounties to raise troops, Wang Jian went on his own and was enrolled as a military scout.

sentences.zh: 廣明中，黃巢陷長安，僖宗幸蜀。

translations.literal: In the Guangming era, Huang Chao took Chang'an, and Emperor Xizong went in person to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangming reign, Huang Chao captured Chang'an and Emperor Xizong fled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 時梁祖為巢將，領眾攻襄、鄧，宗權遣小校鹿晏宏從監軍楊復光率師攻之，建亦預行。

translations.literal: At the time the Liang founder was a general under Chao, leading troops to attack Xiang and Deng; Zongquan sent the junior officer Lu Yanhong to follow the supervising commander Yang Fuguang in leading an army against him, and Jian also took part in the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The future Liang founder was then one of Huang Chao's generals, leading forces against Xiangyang and Dengzhou. Qin Zongquan sent the junior officer Lu Yanhong with the supervising commander Yang Fuguang to oppose him, and Wang Jian marched with them.

sentences.zh: 是歲，復光入援京師，明年破賊收京城。

translations.literal: That year Fuguang entered to relieve the capital; the next year he broke the rebels and recovered the imperial city.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yang Fuguang marched to relieve the capital; the following year he defeated the rebels and retook the city.

sentences.zh: 初，復光以忠武軍八千人立為八都，晏宏與建各一都校也。

translations.literal: At first Fuguang took eight thousand men of the Zhongwu Army and formed them into eight commands; Yanhong and Jian were each commanders of one command.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fuguang had first organized eight thousand Zhongwu troops into eight commands, with Lu Yanhong and Wang Jian each commanding one.

sentences.zh: 復光死，晏弘率八都迎扈行在，至山南，乃攻剽金、商諸郡縣，得兵數萬，進逼興元，節度使牛叢棄城而去，晏宏因自為留後，建等為屬郡刺史，不令之任。

translations.literal: When Fuguang died, Yanhong led the eight commands to escort the peripatetic court; reaching Shannan, he then raided Jin, Shang, and various prefectures and counties, gaining several tens of thousands of troops and pressing toward Xingyuan; the military governor Niu Cong abandoned the city and fled; Yanhong thereupon made himself acting governor, while Jian and the others were named prefects of subordinate prefectures but not allowed to take office.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Fuguang's death, Lu Yanhong led the eight commands to join the emperor's wandering court. Reaching the Shannan region, he turned to plundering Jinzhou, Shangzhou, and neighboring districts until his forces numbered in the tens of thousands. He then advanced on Xingyuan; Military Governor Niu Cong fled the city, and Yanhong declared himself acting governor. Wang Jian and the others were appointed prefects of subordinate commanderies but were not permitted to take up their posts.

sentences.zh: 俄而晏宏正授節旄，恐部下謀己，多行忍虐，由是部眾離心。

translations.literal: Before long Yanhong received formal investiture with the command baton; fearing that his subordinates would plot against him, he often acted with cruelty, and thereby his troops lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lu Yanhong received formal appointment as military governor. Fearing mutiny among his men, he ruled with increasing cruelty, and his followers began to turn away from him.

sentences.zh: 建與別將韓建友善，晏宏益猜二建，偽待之厚，引入臥內。

translations.literal: Jian was on friendly terms with the other general Han Jian; Yanhong grew ever more suspicious of the two Jians, feigning to treat them generously and bringing them into his private quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was close to another officer named Han Jian. Lu Yanhong grew increasingly suspicious of the two men named Jian, treating them with feigned warmth while summoning them into his private quarters.

sentences.zh: 二建懼，夜登城慰守陴者，因月下共謀所向，謂韓建曰：「僕射甘言厚德，是疑我也，禍難無日矣，早宜擇利而行。」

translations.literal: The two Jians were afraid; at night they climbed the wall to comfort the defenders on the ramparts, and under the moonlight together plotted their course. Wang Jian said to Han Jian, "The Vice Director's sweet words and generous treatment mean he suspects us; disaster is not far off—we should early choose what profits us and act."
translations.idiomatic: Both men were afraid. That night they climbed the wall to encourage the rampart guards, and in the moonlight plotted their next move. Wang Jian said to Han Jian, "His sweet talk and lavish favors mean he suspects us. Disaster cannot be far off—we should choose our advantage and move while we can."

sentences.zh: 韓曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Han said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian said, "Agreed."

sentences.zh: 因率三千人趨行在，僖宗嘉之，賜與巨萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon they led three thousand men to hurry to the peripatetic court; Emperor Xizong commended them and bestowed tens of thousands in gifts.
translations.idiomatic: They then led three thousand men straight to the emperor's camp. Emperor Xizong praised them and rewarded them lavishly.

sentences.zh: 分其兵為五都，仍以舊校主之，即晉暉、李師泰、張造與二建也，因號曰隨駕五都，田令孜皆錄為假子。

translations.literal: Their troops were divided into five commands, still led by the former commanders—namely Jin Hui, Li Shitai, Zhang Zao, and the two Jians—and were therefore called the Five Commands in the Emperor's Train; Tian Lingzi enrolled them all as adoptive sons.
translations.idiomatic: Their force was split into five commands under their former officers—Jin Hui, Li Shitai, Zhang Zao, and the two Jians—and was styled the Five Commands of the Imperial Escort. Tian Lingzi took them all as his adoptive sons.

sentences.zh: 及僖宗還宮，建等分典神策軍，皆遙領刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned to the palace, Jian and the others shared command of the Shence Army, each holding the title of prefect in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital, Wang Jian and the others were given shared command of the Shence Army, each also holding a distant prefectural appointment.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，從僖宗再幸興元，令孜懼逼，求為西川監軍，楊復恭代為觀軍容使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangqi era, following Emperor Xizong on his second journey to Xingyuan, Lingzi, fearing pressure, requested appointment as military supervisor of Xichuan; Yang Fugong replaced him as Commissioner of Army Supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangqi reign, Wang Jian again accompanied Emperor Xizong to Xingyuan. Tian Lingzi, fearing pressure at court, asked to become military supervisor in Xichuan, and Yang Fugong replaced him as Commissioner of Army Supervision.

sentences.zh: 建等素為令孜所厚，復恭懼不附己，乃出五將為郡守，以建為壁州刺史。

translations.literal: Jian and the others had long been favored by Lingzi; Fugong feared they would not attach themselves to him, and therefore sent the five generals out as prefects, appointing Jian prefect of Bi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian and the others had long been favored by Tian Lingzi. Yang Fugong feared they would not side with him, so he posted the five generals as prefects, making Wang Jian prefect of Bi.

sentences.zh: 天子還京，復恭以楊守亮鎮興元，尤畏建侵己，屢召之。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the capital, Fugong stationed Yang Shouliang at Xingyuan and especially feared that Jian would encroach on him, repeatedly summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to the capital, Yang Fugong stationed Yang Shouliang at Xingyuan and especially feared that Wang Jian might threaten his position, summoning him again and again.

sentences.zh: 建不安其郡，因招合溪洞豪猾，有眾八千，寇閬州，陷之，復攻利州，刺史王珙棄城而去。

translations.literal: Jian was ill at ease in his prefecture; he therefore gathered fierce men of the streams and caves, mustering eight thousand troops, raided Lang Prefecture and took it, then attacked Li Prefecture, whose prefect Wang Gong abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Unhappy in his post, Wang Jian rallied fierce leaders from the hill country until he had eight thousand men. He raided Langzhou and captured it, then attacked Lizhou; Prefect Wang Gong abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 建播剽二郡，所至殺掠，守亮不能制。

translations.literal: Jian spread his raids through the two prefectures; wherever he went he killed and plundered, and Shouliang could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian spread terror through both prefectures, killing and looting wherever he went, and Yang Shouliang could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使顧彥朗，初於關輔破賊時與建相聞，每遣人勞問，分貨幣軍食以給之，故建不侵梓、遂。

translations.literal: Gu Yanlang, military governor of Dongchuan, had first become acquainted with Jian when breaking rebels in the Guanzhong region; he often sent men to inquire after him and shared goods, money, and army provisions to supply him, so Jian did not invade Zi and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yanlang, military governor of Dongchuan, had first known Wang Jian when they fought rebels in the Guanzhong region. He regularly sent envoys with gifts and shared supplies with him, and for that reason Wang Jian did not attack Zizhou or Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使陳敬瑄憂其膠固，謀於監軍田令孜，曰：「王八，吾子也，彼無他腸，作賊山南，實進退無歸故也。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan, military governor of Xichuan, worried over his stubborn hold on the region and consulted the military supervisor Tian Lingzi, saying, "Wang the Eighth is my son; he has no other intent—his becoming a bandit in Shannan is truly because he has nowhere to advance or retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan, military governor of Xichuan, worried about Wang Jian's entrenched position and consulted the military supervisor Tian Lingzi. "Wang the Eighth is my adopted son," he said. "He has no other designs. He turned bandit in Shannan only because he had nowhere else to go.

sentences.zh: 吾馳咫尺之書，可以坐置麾下。」

translations.literal: If I send a letter a foot long, I can seat him under my command without stirring."
translations.idiomatic: A short letter from me will bring him into my service without my lifting a finger."

sentences.zh: 即飛書招建。

translations.literal: He immediately sent a swift letter summoning Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He at once sent an urgent summons to Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 建大喜，遣使謂彥朗曰：「監軍阿父遣信見招，仆欲諸成都省阿父，因依陳太師得一大郡，是所願也。」

translations.literal: Jian was greatly pleased and sent an envoy to tell Yanlang, "The military supervisor, my adoptive father, has sent a message summoning me; your servant wishes to go to Chengdu to visit my adoptive father and, relying on Grand Mentor Chen, obtain a large prefecture—that is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was delighted and sent an envoy to Gu Yanlang: "My adoptive father the military supervisor has summoned me. I mean to go to Chengdu to see him and, with Grand Mentor Chen's backing, win a major prefecture—that is what I want."

sentences.zh: 即之梓州見彥朗，留家寄東川，選精甲三千之成都。

translations.literal: He thereupon went to Zizhou to see Yanlang, left his family in Dongchuan's care, selected three thousand picked armored troops, and marched to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He went at once to Zizhou to see Gu Yanlang, left his family in Dongchuan's care, chose three thousand elite troops, and set out for Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 行次鹿頭，或謂敬瑄曰：「建，今之劇賊，鴟視狼顧，專謀人國邑，儻其即至，公以何等處之？

translations.literal: When he reached Lútóu Pass, someone said to Jingxuan, "Jian is today's fierce bandit—he looks like an owl and glances like a wolf, bent solely on seizing others' states and cities. If he should soon arrive, how will you deal with him?
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian reached Lutou Pass, someone warned Chen Jingxuan: "Wang Jian is the fiercest rebel of the day—rapacious and watchful, bent on seizing others' domains. If he arrives soon, how will you receive him?

sentences.zh: 彼建雄心，終不居人之下，公如以將校遇之，是養虎自貽其患也。」

translations.literal: That Jian has a great heart and will never remain beneath others; if you treat him as a mere general or colonel, you are rearing a tiger and bringing disaster on yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian has grand ambitions and will never serve under another. If you treat him as an ordinary officer, you are raising a tiger that will bring ruin on you.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄懼，乃遣人止建，遽修城守。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was afraid and sent men to stop Jian, hastily repairing the walls for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan was alarmed, sent men to halt Wang Jian, and hurriedly strengthened the city's defenses.

sentences.zh: 建怒，遂據漢州，領輕兵至成都。

translations.literal: Jian was enraged, thereupon seized Han Prefecture, and led light troops to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian flew into a rage, seized Hanzhou, and led light troops straight to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄讓之曰：「若何為者，而犯吾疆理？」

translations.literal: Jingxuan reproached him, saying, "What are you doing, encroaching on my borders?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan rebuked him: "What do you think you are doing, violating my territory?

sentences.zh: 建軍吏報曰：「閬州司徒比寄東川，而軍容太師使者繼召，今復拒絕，何也？

translations.literal: Jian's military clerk replied, "The Minister of Lang Prefecture recently entrusted his household to Dongchuan, while the Army Supervisor Grand Mentor's envoys summoned him again and again; now you refuse him—why?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian's officer answered: "Your Minister of Langzhou lately left his family in Dongchuan's care, and the Army Supervisor Grand Mentor's envoys summoned him repeatedly. Why refuse him now?

sentences.zh: 司徒不惜改轅而東，來北省太師，反為拒絕，慮顧梓州復相嫌間，謂我何心故也。

translations.literal: The Minister did not begrudge turning his carriage east to come north and visit the Grand Mentor, yet was refused in return; he fears that Gu at Zizhou will again be estranged and will wonder what intent moves us.
translations.idiomatic: He did not hesitate to turn east and come north to see the Grand Mentor, only to be turned away. He fears Gu Yanlang at Zizhou will take offense again and wonder what we mean by this.

sentences.zh: 使我來報，且欲寄食漢州，公勿復疑。」

translations.literal: He sent me to report and also wishes to quarter his troops at Han Prefecture—do not doubt further."
translations.idiomatic: He sent me to say that he only seeks to provision his men at Hanzhou—please harbor no further suspicion."

sentences.zh: 時光啟三年。

translations.literal: It was the third year of Guangqi.
translations.idiomatic: It was the third year of the Guangqi reign.

sentences.zh: 居浹旬，建盡取東川之眾，設梯沖攻成都，三日不克而退，復保漢州。

translations.literal: Within ten days Jian gathered all the forces of Dongchuan, set up scaling ladders and battering rams, and attacked Chengdu; after three days he could not take it and withdrew, again holding Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Wang Jian mustered all the troops Gu Yanlang could spare, raised siege ladders and rams, and assaulted Chengdu. After three days he failed and withdrew, again holding Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 月餘，大剽蜀土，進逼彭州，百道攻之，敬瑄出兵來援，建解圍，縱兵大掠，十一州皆罹其毒，民不聊生。

translations.literal: After more than a month he raided broadly through Shu territory, advanced and pressed Peng Prefecture, attacking from a hundred directions; Jingxuan sent troops to relieve it; Jian lifted the siege and let his army plunder on a great scale—eleven prefectures all suffered his ravages, and the people could not live.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a month he ravaged Shu, advanced on Pengzhou, and attacked from every side. Chen Jingxuan sent relief; Wang Jian raised the siege and unleashed his troops in a great pillage. Eleven prefectures suffered his depredations, and the people could barely survive.

sentences.zh: 建軍勢日盛，復攻成都，敬瑄患之，顧彥朗亦懼侵己。

translations.literal: Jian's military power grew daily; he again attacked Chengdu; Jingxuan was troubled by it, and Gu Yanlang also feared he would encroach on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian's power grew daily. He attacked Chengdu again. Chen Jingxuan was alarmed, and Gu Yanlang feared he would be next.

sentences.zh: 昭宗即位，彥朗表請雪建，擇大臣為蜀帥，移敬瑄他鎮，乃詔宰臣韋昭度鎮蜀，以代敬瑄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong took the throne, Yanlang memorialized requesting that Jian be cleared, that a great minister be chosen as commander of Shu, and that Jingxuan be transferred to another post; the court then ordered the chief minister Wei Zhaodu to take command of Shu in place of Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong came to the throne, Gu Yanlang memorialized asking that Wang Jian be pardoned, that a senior minister be sent to command Shu, and that Chen Jingxuan be transferred elsewhere. The court appointed Chief Minister Wei Zhaodu military governor of Shu to replace him.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄不受代，天子怒，命顧彥朗、楊守亮討之，時昭度以建為牙內都校，董其部兵。

translations.literal: Jingxuan would not accept replacement; the Son of Heaven was angry and ordered Gu Yanlang and Yang Shouliang to attack him; at the time Zhaodu made Jian commander of the palace guard and supervised his division troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan refused to step down. The emperor was furious and ordered Gu Yanlang and Yang Shouliang to attack him. Wei Zhaodu meanwhile made Wang Jian commander of the palace guard and put him in charge of his own troops.

sentences.zh: 〈（《鑒戒錄》云：昭度以部兵置行府。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Record of Mirrors and Warnings》 says: Zhaodu established his field headquarters with his division troops.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Record of Mirrors and Warnings》 states that Wei Zhaodu set up his field headquarters with his division troops.)〉

sentences.zh: 及王師無功，建謂昭度曰：「相公興數萬之眾，討賊未效，餉運交不相屬。

translations.literal: When the imperial army achieved nothing, Jian said to Zhaodu, "Your Excellency raised tens of thousands of men to punish the rebel without effect, and supply transports do not link up one with another.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial campaign failed, Wang Jian told Wei Zhaodu, "Your Excellency raised tens of thousands of men to punish the rebel without success, and supplies no longer keep pace.

sentences.zh: 近聞遷洛以來，藩鎮相噬，朝廷姑息不暇，與其勞師以事蠻方，不如從而赦之，且以兵威靖中原，是國之本也。

translations.literal: I have lately heard that since the move to Luoyang the military governors have devoured one another and the court has had no leisure to indulge them; rather than wear out the army on the southern barbarians, it would be better to follow by pardoning him and use military might to pacify the central plains—that is the foundation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Since the court moved to Luoyang, the military governors have been tearing one another apart and the throne has barely kept up. Rather than exhaust your army in the south, it would be better to pardon him and turn your strength to pacifying the central plains—that is the foundation of the realm.

sentences.zh: 相公盍歸朝覲，與主上畫之。」

translations.literal: Why does Your Excellency not return to court to have an audience and plan it with the sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Why not return to court and lay the matter before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 昭度持疑未決。

translations.literal: Zhaodu hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaodu hesitated, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 一日，建陰令軍士於行府門外擒昭度親吏，臠而食之，建徐啟昭度曰：「蓋軍士乏食，以至於是耶！」

translations.literal: One day Jian secretly ordered soldiers outside the field headquarters gate to seize Zhaodu's personal clerk, cut him to pieces, and eat him; Jian then slowly informed Zhaodu, "Perhaps the soldiers lacked food and came to this!"
translations.idiomatic: One day Wang Jian secretly had his soldiers seize Wei Zhaodu's personal clerk outside headquarters, butcher him, and eat him. Wang Jian then told Wei Zhaodu calmly, "I suppose the men were simply out of food and driven to this!

sentences.zh: 昭度大懼，遂留符節與建，即日東還。

translations.literal: Zhaodu was greatly afraid, left his tally and baton with Jian, and that same day returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Wei Zhaodu left his credentials with Wang Jian and returned east the same day.

sentences.zh: 才出劍門，建即嚴兵守門，不納東師。

translations.literal: He had only just passed Jianmen Pass when Jian immediately stationed troops in strength to guard the gate and would not admit the eastern army.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he passed Jianmen Pass when Wang Jian sealed the gate with a strong garrison and refused entry to the eastern army.

sentences.zh: 月餘，建攻西川管內八州，所至響應，遂急攻成都，田令孜登城謂建曰：「老夫與八哥相厚，太師久以知聞，有何嫌恨，如是困我之甚耶！」

translations.literal: After more than a month Jian attacked the eight prefectures within Xichuan's jurisdiction; wherever he went there was response, and he then pressed the attack on Chengdu. Tian Lingzi mounted the wall and said to Jian, "This old man and Brother the Eighth have long been close; the Grand Mentor has known it for long—what grudge is there, that you should distress me so severely!"
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month Wang Jian attacked eight prefectures under Xichuan's control, meeting support everywhere, then pressed hard on Chengdu. Tian Lingzi mounted the wall and called to him: "Brother the Eighth and I have always been close, and the Grand Mentor has long known it. What grudge drives you to besiege me so fiercely!

sentences.zh: 建曰：「軍容父子之恩，心何敢忘，但天子付以兵柄，太師孤絕朝廷故也。

translations.literal: Jian said, "The Army Supervisor's father-and-son kindness—how would I dare forget it in my heart? But the Son of Heaven entrusted you with the military command, and the Grand Mentor has isolated himself from the court—that is why.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian replied, "How could I forget the bond between father and son that we share? But the emperor gave you the army, and you have cut yourself off from the court—that is the trouble.

sentences.zh: 茍太師悉心改圖，何福如之！」

translations.literal: If the Grand Mentor would wholeheartedly change his course, what blessing could equal it!"
translations.idiomatic: If you would wholeheartedly change course, what blessing could be greater!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「吾欲與八哥軍中相款，如何？」

translations.literal: He also said, "I wish to entertain Brother the Eighth in the army—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: He added, "I would like to entertain you in camp, Brother the Eighth—what do you say?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「父子之義，何嫌也。」

translations.literal: He said, "In the bond of father and son, what scruple is there."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian answered, "Between father and son, what need for scruple."

sentences.zh: 是夜，令孜攜蜀帥符印入建軍授建。

translations.literal: That night Lingzi carried the tally and seal of the Shu commander into Jian's camp and handed them to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: That night Tian Lingzi brought the commander's tally and seal into Wang Jian's camp and surrendered them.

sentences.zh: 建泣謝曰：「太師初心太過，致有今日相戾，既此推心，一切如舊。」

translations.literal: Jian wept and thanked him, saying, "The Grand Mentor's original intent went too far and brought about today's estrangement; now that you have opened your heart, all is as before."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian wept and thanked him: "Your first resolve went too far and brought us to this breach. Now that you have opened your heart to me, all shall be as before.

sentences.zh: 翌日，敬瑄啟關迎建，以蜀帥讓之，建乃自稱留後，表陳其事。

translations.literal: The next day Jingxuan opened the gate to welcome Jian and yielded the Shu command to him; Jian thereupon styled himself acting governor and memorialized stating the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chen Jingxuan opened the gates to receive him and yielded command of Shu. Wang Jian declared himself acting governor and memorialized the court.

sentences.zh: 明年春，制授檢校太傅、成都尹、西川節度副大使知節度事、管內觀察處置、雲南八國招撫等使，時龍紀元年也。

translations.literal: The next spring an edict appointed him honorary Grand Tutor, Prefect of Chengdu, deputy military governor of Xichuan with full authority over military affairs, commissioner for observation and disposition within the circuit, and commissioner for pacifying the eight kingdoms of Yunnan—it was the first year of Longji.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring the throne appointed him Honorary Grand Tutor, Prefect of Chengdu, and full military governor of Xichuan with authority over observation, disposition, and pacification of Yunnan—it was the first year of the Longji reign.

sentences.zh: 移敬瑄於雅州安置，仍以其子為刺史，既行，建令人殺之於路，令孜仍舊監軍事。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was transferred to be settled at Ya Prefecture, and his son was still made prefect; once they had set out, Jian had men kill them on the road; Lingzi continued as before in supervising military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan was sent into retirement at Yazhou, with his son appointed prefect there. Once they had departed, Wang Jian had them killed on the road. Tian Lingzi continued as military supervisor.

sentences.zh: 數月，或告令孜通鳳翔書問，下獄餓死。

translations.literal: Several months later someone reported that Lingzi was exchanging letters with Fengxiang; he was imprisoned and starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Months later someone accused Tian Lingzi of corresponding with Fengxiang. He was thrown into prison and starved to death.

sentences.zh: 〈（《蜀梼杌》云：「敬瑄廢處雅州，以其子為刺史。

translations.literal: (The 《Annals of Shu》 says: "Jingxuan was deposed and settled at Ya Prefecture, and his son was made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Annals of Shu》 records: "Chen Jingxuan was deposed and sent to Yazhou, with his son made prefect there.

sentences.zh: 既行，建遣殺於三江，令孜仍監其軍，復以令孜陰附鳳翔，下獄餓死。）〉

translations.literal: Once they had set out, Jian sent men to kill them at Sanjiang; Lingzi still supervised his army; again because Lingzi secretly attached himself to Fengxiang, he was imprisoned and starved to death.")〉
translations.idiomatic: Once they had departed, Wang Jian had them killed at Sanjiang. Tian Lingzi continued to supervise the army until he was accused of secretly siding with Fengxiang and was imprisoned and starved to death.")〉

sentences.zh: 建雄猜多機略，意常難測，既有蜀土，復欲窺伺東川，又以彥朗婚姻之舊，未果行。

translations.literal: Jian was fierce, suspicious, and full of stratagems; his intent was often hard to fathom. Once he held Shu territory he again wished to spy out Dongchuan, but because of his old marriage tie with Yanlang he did not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was fierce, suspicious, and endlessly scheming; his intentions were often impossible to read. Once he held Shu he again cast his eye on Dongchuan, but because of his old marriage tie with Gu Yanlang he held back.

sentences.zh: 會彥朗卒，弟彥暉代為梓帥，交情稍怠。

translations.literal: When Yanlang died, his younger brother Yanhui succeeded as commander of Zi and their friendship cooled somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu Yanlang died, his younger brother Yanhui became commander at Zizhou, and their friendship cooled.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞乘其有間，密構彥暉，因與茂貞連盟，關征疆吏之間，與蜀人得失。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen seized the opening and secretly won over Yanhui; he therefore allied with Maozhen, and at the passes and border posts the officials contended with the people of Shu for gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen seized the opening and secretly won Yanhui over. Yanhui allied with him, and at the passes and border posts their officials and Shu agents wrestled for advantage.

sentences.zh: 大順末，建出師攻梓州，彥暉求援於鳳翔，李茂貞出師援之，建即圍解，自是秦、川交惡者累年。

translations.literal: At the end of Dashun, Jian marched out to attack Zizhou; Yanhui sought aid from Fengxiang, and Li Maozhen marched out to relieve him; Jian thereupon lifted the siege; from this Qin and Chuan were at enmity for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dashun reign Wang Jian attacked Zizhou. Yanhui sought help from Fengxiang, and Li Maozhen marched to his relief, forcing Wang Jian to raise the siege. From then on Qin and Shu were enemies for years.

sentences.zh: 後建大起蜀軍，敗岐、梓之兵於利州，彥暉懼，乞和，請與岐人絕，許之。

translations.literal: Later Jian raised a great Shu army and defeated the Qi and Zi forces at Li Prefecture; Yanhui was afraid, begged for peace, and asked to break with the Qi people; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Jian raised a great Shu army and defeated the Fengxiang and Zizhou forces at Lizhou. Yanhui was terrified, sued for peace, and asked to break with Fengxiang; Wang Jian agreed.

sentences.zh: 景福中，山南之師寇東川，彥暉求援於建，建出兵赴之，大敗興元之眾。

translations.literal: In the Jingfu era the Shannan army invaded Dongchuan; Yanhui sought aid from Jian; Jian sent troops to his relief and greatly defeated the Xingyuan host.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingfu reign the Shannan army invaded Dongchuan. Yanhui asked Wang Jian for help; he marched out and routed the Xingyuan forces.

sentences.zh: 洎軍旋，建承虛奄襲梓州，據彥暉，置於成都，遂兼有兩川，自此軍鋒益熾。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Jian took advantage of the moment to launch a sudden attack on Zizhou, seized Yanhui, and placed him in Chengdu; he thereby held both Chuan together, and from this his military edge grew ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: When his army returned, Wang Jian seized the moment to strike Zizhou, captured Yanhui, and kept him in Chengdu. He now held both river basins, and his military power grew fiercer still.

sentences.zh: 天復初，李茂貞、韓全誨劫遷車駕在鳳翔，梁祖攻圍歷年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, Li Maozhen and Han Quanhui seized and moved the imperial carriage to Fengxiang; the Liang founder besieged them for years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu reign Li Maozhen and Han Quanhui seized the emperor and held him at Fengxiang. The Liang founder besieged them for years.

sentences.zh: 建外修好於汴，指茂貞罪狀，又陰與茂貞間使往來，且言堅壁勿和，許以出師赴援，因分命諸軍攻取興元。

translations.literal: Outwardly Jian cultivated good relations with Bian, denouncing Maozhen's crimes; secretly he exchanged envoys with Maozhen, telling him to hold the walls and not make peace, promising to march out in relief, and meanwhile ordering his various armies to attack and take Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Wang Jian courted Bian while denouncing Li Maozhen's crimes. In secret he exchanged envoys with Maozhen, urging him to hold firm and refuse peace while promising relief, even as he ordered his armies to seize Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 比及梁祖解圍，茂貞山南諸州皆為建所有，自置守將。

translations.literal: By the time the Liang founder lifted the siege, Maozhen's Shannan prefectures were all in Jian's possession, and he himself appointed garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the Liang founder lifted the siege, all of Maozhen's Shannan prefectures belonged to Wang Jian, who appointed his own garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 及茂貞垂翅，天子遷雒陽，建復攻茂貞之秦、隴等州，茂貞削弱不能守。

translations.literal: When Maozhen's wings were clipped and the Son of Heaven moved to Luoyang, Jian again attacked Maozhen's Qin, Long, and other prefectures; Maozhen was weakened and could not hold them.
translations.idiomatic: When Maozhen's power collapsed and the emperor moved to Luoyang, Wang Jian again attacked his Qinzhou, Longzhou, and other holdings. Maozhen was too weak to defend them.

sentences.zh: 或勸建因取鳳翔，建曰：「此言失策，吾所得已多，不俟復增岐下。

translations.literal: Someone urged Jian to take Fengxiang in the course of events; Jian said, "This counsel misses the mark—I have already gained much and need not add more under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Wang Jian to seize Fengxiang while he could. He said, "That would be a mistake. I have already gained enough and need not add more territory under Qi.

sentences.zh: 茂貞雖常才，然名望宿素，與朱公力爭不足，守境有餘。

translations.literal: Maozhen may be only ordinary in talent, yet his fame is long established; he is not equal to contending in strength with Lord Zhu, but he has more than enough to guard his borders.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen is only a man of ordinary talent, but his name is old and weighty. He cannot match Lord Zhu in force, yet he has more than enough to hold his borders.

sentences.zh: 韓生所謂入為扞蔽，出為席藉是也。

translations.literal: This is what Master Han meant by serving within as a shield and screen and serving without as mat and cushion.
translations.idiomatic: This is what Han Feizi meant by a shield within and a mat without.

sentences.zh: 適宜援而固之，為吾盾鹵耳。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to support and strengthen him and make him my shield and rampart."
translations.idiomatic: The right move is to support and strengthen him as my shield and rampart.

sentences.zh: 及梁祖將謀強禪，建與諸藩同謀興復，乃令其將康晏率兵三萬會於鳳翔，數與汴將王重師戰，不利而還。

translations.literal: When the Liang founder was about to plot forced abdication, Jian joined the various governors in plotting restoration and ordered his general Kang Yan to lead thirty thousand men to assemble at Fengxiang; he fought several times with the Bian general Wang Chongshi, fared ill, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang founder prepared to seize the throne by force, Wang Jian joined the other governors in plotting restoration and sent his general Kang Yan with thirty thousand men to Fengxiang. Kang Yan fought several engagements with the Bian general Wang Chongshi, fared poorly, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 趙匡凝之失荊、襄也，弟匡明以其幹奔蜀，建因得夔、峽、忠、萬等州。

translations.literal: When Zhao Kuangning lost Jing and Xiang, his younger brother Kuangming fled to Shu with his staff; Jian thereby gained Qí, Xiá, Zhōng, Wàn, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Kuangning lost Jingzhou and Xiangzhou, his younger brother Kuangming fled to Shu with his staff. Wang Jian thereby gained Kuizhou, Xiazhou, Zhongzhou, Wanzhou, and others.

sentences.zh: 及梁祖開國，蜀人請建行劉備故事。

translations.literal: When the Liang founder founded his state, the people of Shu asked Jian to follow Liu Bei's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang founder founded his dynasty, the people of Shu urged Wang Jian to follow Liu Bei's example and declare himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 建自帝於成都，改元永平。

translations.literal: Jian declared himself emperor at Chengdu and changed the era name to Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian declared himself emperor at Chengdu and adopted the era name Yongping.

sentences.zh: 五年，改元通正。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he changed the era name to Tongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In his fifth year he changed the era name to Tongzheng.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，改元天漢，又改元光天。

translations.literal: That winter he changed the era name to Tianhan, and again to Guangtian.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he changed the era name to Tianhan, then again to Guangtian.

sentences.zh: 在位十二年，年七十二。

translations.literal: He reigned twelve years and died at seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned twelve years and died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子衍嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 衍，建之幼子也。

translations.literal: Yan was Jian's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Wang Jian's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 建卒，衍襲偽位，改元乾德。

translations.literal: When Jian died, Yan inherited the usurper's throne and changed the era name to Qiande.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian died, Yan took the throne and adopted the era name Qiande.

sentences.zh: 六年十二月，改明年為鹹康。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year he changed the next year to Xian'kang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of his sixth year he renamed the coming year Xian'kang.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，衍奉其母、徐妃同遊於青城山，駐於上清宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Yan accompanied his mother and Consort Xu on a tour of Mount Qingcheng and lodged at the Shangqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yan took his mother and Consort Xu on an excursion to Mount Qingcheng and stayed at the Shangqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 時宮人皆衣道服，頂金蓮花冠，衣畫雲霞，望之若神仙，及侍宴，酒酣，皆免冠而退，則其髻髽然。

translations.literal: At the time the palace women all wore Daoist robes, topped with golden lotus crowns and robes painted with cloud and mist; viewed from afar they seemed immortals; when they attended the banquet and the wine was deep they all removed their caps and withdrew, and then their topknots stood bare.
translations.idiomatic: The palace women all wore Daoist robes and golden lotus crowns, their garments painted with clouds and mist so that from a distance they looked like immortals. When they served at the banquet and the wine ran deep, they removed their caps to withdraw, revealing their bare topknots.

sentences.zh: 又構怡神亭，以佞臣韓昭等為狎客，雜以婦人，以恣荒宴，或自旦至暮，繼之以燭。

translations.literal: He also built the Pleasing-the-Spirit Pavilion, taking the sycophant Han Zhao and others as intimate guests, mixing in women, to indulge in dissolute feasting—sometimes from dawn to dusk, continuing with candles.
translations.idiomatic: He also built the Pleasing-the-Spirit Pavilion, where sycophants such as Han Zhao served as his boon companions amid a crowd of women, feasting without restraint from dawn to dusk, one round of candles following another.

sentences.zh: 偽嘉王宗壽侍宴，因以社稷國政為言，言發涕流，至於再三。

translations.literal: The usurper Prince of Jia, Zongshou, attended the banquet and spoke of the altars of state and national affairs; as he spoke tears flowed, and this happened again and again.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jia, Zongshou, attended the banquet and spoke of the realm and its governance, weeping as he spoke, again and again.

sentences.zh: 同宴佞臣潘在迎等並奏衍云：「嘉王好酒悲。」

translations.literal: The sycophants at the same banquet, Pan Zaiying and others, all reported to Yan, saying, "The Prince of Jia is fond of wine and given to grief."
translations.idiomatic: The sycophants at the table, Pan Zaiying and the rest, told Yan together, "The Prince of Jia loves his wine and loves his tears.

sentences.zh: 因翻恣諧謔，取笑而罷。

translations.literal: They thereupon turned to unrestrained jest and banter, making sport and dismissing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: They then turned to coarse jokes and ridicule until the moment passed.

sentences.zh: 自是忠正之臣結舌矣。

translations.literal: From this loyal and upright ministers held their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: From then on loyal ministers held their tongues.

sentences.zh: 時中國多故，衍得以自安。

translations.literal: At the time the central realm had many troubles, and Yan was able to remain at ease.
translations.idiomatic: With turmoil rampant across the central realm, Yan was left undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗平梁，遣使告捷於蜀，蜀人恟懼，致禮復命，稱「大蜀國主致書上大唐皇帝」，詞理稍抗，莊宗不能容，遣客省使李嚴報聘，且市宮中珍玩，蜀人皆禁而不出。

translations.literal: Tang Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Liang and sent envoys to announce victory to Shu; the people of Shu were alarmed and fearful, sent gifts in reply, and styled their message "The Lord of Great Shu writes to present to the Emperor of Great Tang"—the wording was somewhat defiant; Zhuangzong could not tolerate it and sent the guest-house envoy Li Yan on a return mission, also wishing to purchase rare treasures from the palace; the people of Shu all forbade their sale and would not release them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, he sent envoys to announce victory in Shu. The Shu court was alarmed and replied with gifts, addressing their letter "The Lord of Great Shu writes to the Emperor of Great Tang"—wording Zhuangzong found insolent. He sent the guest-house envoy Li Yan on a return mission and sought to buy palace treasures; the Shu authorities refused to let any leave.

sentences.zh: 衍既沖呆，軍國之政，鹹委於人。

translations.literal: Yan being dull and simple-minded, military and state affairs were all entrusted to others.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was dull and childish, and he left all military and civil affairs to others.

sentences.zh: 有王宗弼者，為六軍使，總外任；

translations.literal: There was one Wang Zongbi, who served as commander of the Six Armies and oversaw external appointments;
translations.idiomatic: One Wang Zongbi served as commander of the Six Armies and controlled external appointments;

sentences.zh: 宋光嗣者，為樞密使，總內任。

translations.literal: Song Guangsi served as Commissioner of Confidential Affairs and oversaw internal appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Song Guangsi served as Commissioner of Confidential Affairs and controlled internal appointments.

sentences.zh: 洎嚴至蜀，光嗣等曲宴，因言中國近事，嚴亦引近事折之，語在嚴傳。

translations.literal: When Yan came to Shu, Guangsi and others gave a private banquet and spoke of recent affairs in the central realm; Yan also cited recent events to refute them—the account is in Yan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yan reached Shu, Guangsi and his circle entertained him privately and spoke of recent events in the central realm. Yan answered with recent events of his own to refute them; the full account appears in Yan's biography.

sentences.zh: 光嗣等聞嚴辯對，畏而奇之。

translations.literal: Guangsi and the others heard Yan's skilled replies and were both afraid and amazed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi and the others heard Yan's sharp replies and were both afraid and impressed.

sentences.zh: 及嚴使還，奏莊宗曰：「王衍呆童耳，宗弼等總其兵柄，但益家財，不恤民事，君臣上下，惟務窮奢。

translations.literal: When Yan returned from his mission he reported to Zhuangzong, saying, "Wang Yan is but a dull child; Zongbi and others hold all military power, only increasing family wealth and caring nothing for the people's affairs; ruler and ministers above and below devote themselves solely to extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan returned he reported to Emperor Zhuangzong: "Wang Yan is a foolish boy. Zongbi and the rest hold all military power, enriching their families while ignoring the people. From top to bottom the court cares only for extravagance.

sentences.zh: 其舊勛故老，棄而不任，蠻蜓蜑之人，痛深瘡痏。

translations.literal: The old meritorious ministers are cast aside and not employed; the Man, Ting, and Dan peoples suffer wounds deep as festering sores.
translations.idiomatic: Old ministers of merit are cast aside and unused, while the tribal peoples of the south bear wounds as grievous as open sores.

sentences.zh: 以臣料之，大兵一臨，望風瓦解。」

translations.literal: By your servant's estimate, when the great army arrives they will crumble at the first wind."
translations.idiomatic: In my judgment, when the imperial army arrives they will collapse at the first blow.

sentences.zh: 莊宗深然之，遂蒐兵括馬，有平蜀之志。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong deeply approved this and thereupon gathered troops and rounded up horses, cherishing the ambition to pacify Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong strongly agreed and began gathering troops and horses, resolved to conquer Shu.

sentences.zh: 唐師未起時，偽東川節度使宋承葆獻計於衍云：「唐國兵強，不早為謀，後將焉救？

translations.literal: Before the Tang army set out, the usurper military governor of Dongchuan Song Chengbao presented a plan to Yan, saying, "The Tang state is strong in arms—if we do not plan early, how will we be saved later?
translations.idiomatic: Before the Tang army marched, the Shu military governor of Dongchuan Song Chengbao urged Yan: "Tang is militarily strong. If we do not act now, how will we be saved later?

sentences.zh: 請於嘉州沿江造戰艦五百艘，募水軍五千，自江下峽，臣以東師出襄、鄧，水陸俱進，東北沿邊，嚴兵據險。

translations.literal: I ask that five hundred warships be built along the river at Jia Prefecture, five thousand naval troops recruited, and that they descend the river through the gorges while your servant leads eastern forces out from Xiang and Deng—advancing by land and water together, with strict troops holding the passes along the northeast frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Build five hundred warships at Jiazhou along the river and recruit five thousand sailors to descend through the gorges. I will lead eastern forces from Xiangyang and Dengzhou. Land and water forces will advance together, with strong garrisons holding the northeastern passes.

sentences.zh: 南師出江陵，利則進取，否則退保硤口。

translations.literal: Southern forces will issue from Jiangling—if advantageous they will advance and seize ground; if not, they will withdraw and hold Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Southern forces will march from Jiangling, advancing when the advantage is ours and falling back to hold Xiakou if not.

sentences.zh: 又選三蜀驍壯三萬，急攻岐、雍，東據河、潼，北招契丹，啖以美利，見可則進，否則據散關以固吾圉，事縱不捷，亦攻敵人之心矣。」

translations.literal: Further select thirty thousand fierce stalwarts of the Three Shu, swiftly attack Qi and Yong, hold east the He and Tong regions, recruit the Khitan in the north with tempting profit—advance when you see opportunity, otherwise hold Sanguan Pass to secure our borders; even if the affair does not succeed, it will still strike at the enemy's heart."
translations.idiomatic: Further, choose thirty thousand elite troops from the Three Shu, strike quickly at Qi and Yong, seize the east at the Yellow River and Tong Pass, and entice the Khitans in the north with rich rewards. Advance when you can; otherwise hold Sanguan Pass to secure our borders. Even if we do not win outright, we will shake the enemy's resolve.

sentences.zh: 衍不從。

translations.literal: Yan did not follow this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yan refused to follow this advice.

sentences.zh: 唐同光三年九月十日，莊宗下制伐蜀，命興聖宮使魏王繼岌為都統，樞密使郭崇韜為行營都招討。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the ninth month of the third year of Tongguang in Tang, Zhuangzong issued an edict to attack Shu, appointing the Prince of Wei Jiji, Commissioner of the Xingsheng Palace, as supreme commander, and the Commissioner of Confidential Affairs Guo Chongtao as overall commander of the campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the ninth month of Tongguang year 3, Emperor Zhuangzong ordered an expedition against Shu, naming Prince of Wei Jiji supreme commander and Commissioner of Confidential Affairs Guo Chongtao overall field commander.

sentences.zh: 其月十八日，魏王統闕下諸軍發洛陽。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of that month the Prince of Wei led the armies of the court from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth of that month the Prince of Wei led the imperial armies out of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月二十一日，魏王至德陽，衍報云：「比與將校謀歸國，偽樞密使宋光嗣、景潤澄，南北院宣徽使李周輅、歐陽晃等四人異謀熒惑，臣各已處斬，今送納首級。」

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month the Prince of Wei reached Deyang; Yan reported, saying, "Lately I plotted with generals and colonels to return to the empire; the usurper Commissioners of Confidential Affairs Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng, and the Commissioners of Palace Affairs of the Northern and Southern Bureaus Li Zhou'e and Ouyang Huang—the four of them with divergent plots misled and confused matters; your servant has executed each of them and now sends their heads."
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first of the eleventh month the Prince of Wei reached Deyang. Yan reported: "I had lately plotted with my officers to surrender to the empire, but the Commissioners of Confidential Affairs Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng and the palace commissioners Li Zhou'e and Ouyang Huang led me astray with contrary counsel. I have executed all four and now send their heads.

sentences.zh: 是日，衍上表曰：「臣衍先人建，久在坤維，受先朝寵澤，一開土宇，將四十年。

translations.literal: That same day Yan submitted a memorial, saying, "Your servant Yan's forebear Jian long dwelt in the southwest, received the former dynasty's favor, opened a domain, and has held it for nearly forty years.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Yan submitted a memorial: "My forebear Wang Jian long held the southwest, received the former dynasty's favor, and opened a domain that has stood for nearly forty years.

sentences.zh: 頃以梁孽興災，洪圖版蕩，不可助逆，遂乃從權，勉徇眾情，止王三旬，固非獲已，未有所歸。

translations.literal: Recently because the Liang villain brought disaster and the great design was shaken, one could not aid rebellion; I therefore followed expediency and reluctantly yielded to popular sentiment, reigning as king for only thirty days—it was truly not my wish, and I had nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang usurper brought calamity and the empire was shaken, I could not aid rebellion. I yielded to expediency and popular pressure, reigning as king for only thirty days—not from choice, but because I had nowhere else to turn.

sentences.zh: 臣輒紹鎡基，且安生聚。

translations.literal: Your servant thereupon inherited the foundation and sought to settle the people's livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: I then inherited his foundation and sought only to settle the people.

sentences.zh: 臣衍誠惶誠恐，伏惟皇帝陛下，嗣堯、舜之業，陳湯、武之師，廓定寰區，削平兇逆，梯航垂集，文軌混同。

translations.literal: Your servant Yan is truly fearful and trembling; I bow before Your Majesty the Emperor, who succeeds the enterprise of Yao and Shun, arrays the armies of Tang and Wu, clears and settles all within the four seas, cuts down the violent and rebellious, gathers tribute by ladder-ships and river craft, and unifies writing and cart-tracks.
translations.idiomatic: I am filled with fear and trembling before Your Majesty, who inherits the legacy of Yao and Shun, marshals armies like those of the Shang founders, pacifies the realm, destroys the wicked, gathers tribute from every quarter, and unifies the empire under one order.

sentences.zh: 臣方議改圖，便期納款，遽聞王師致討，實抱驚危。

translations.literal: Your servant was just discussing changing course and expected soon to offer submission, when suddenly I heard that the imperial army had come to punish me—I am truly alarmed and in peril.
translations.idiomatic: I was just planning to change course and offer submission when suddenly I learned that the imperial army had come against me. I am truly alarmed and in peril.

sentences.zh: 今則將千里之封疆，盡為王土；

translations.literal: Now a thousand-li of territory shall all become the King's land;
translations.idiomatic: Now a thousand li of territory shall all become imperial soil;

sentences.zh: 冀萬家之臣妾，皆沭皇恩。

translations.literal: I hope that the subjects and households of ten thousand families may all bathe in imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: and I hope that countless households may all receive the emperor's grace.

sentences.zh: 必當輿櫬乞降，負荊請命。

translations.literal: I shall surely come bearing my coffin to beg surrender and carry thorns to plead for my life.
translations.idiomatic: I shall surely come bearing my coffin to beg surrender and carrying thorns to plead for my life.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下，回照臨之造，施覆幬之仁，別示哀矜，以安反側。

translations.literal: I bow before Your Majesty the Emperor to turn back the grace of your nurturing care, extend the benevolence of your covering canopy, and show special pity to settle those who waver.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to look back on the grace of your nurturing care, extend the mercy of your protecting canopy, and show special compassion to settle those who waver.

sentences.zh: 儻墳塋而獲祀，實存沒以知歸，臣無任望恩虔禱之至。

translations.literal: If my ancestral tombs may receive sacrifice, it will truly let the living and dead know where they belong; your servant cannot bear the weight of hoping for grace and prays with utmost devotion.
translations.idiomatic: If my ancestral tombs may still receive sacrifice, the living and dead will know where they belong. I cannot express my gratitude and pray with utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 乙酉年十一月日，臣王衍上表。」

translations.literal: On a day of the eleventh month of the yiyou year, your servant Wang Yan submits this memorial."
translations.idiomatic: On a day in the eleventh month of the yiyou year, your servant Wang Yan submits this memorial.

sentences.zh: 其月二十七日，魏王至成都北五里升仙橋，偽百官班於橋下，衍乘行輿至，素衣白馬，牽羊，草索系首，面縛銜璧，輿櫬於後。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day of that month the Prince of Wei reached Ascension-to-Immortals Bridge five li north of Chengdu; the usurper officials formed ranks below the bridge; Yan came in a traveling carriage, in plain white garments on a white horse, leading a sheep, with a grass rope about his neck, bound face-forward holding a jade disk, with a coffin borne behind on a carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh of that month the Prince of Wei reached Ascension Bridge five li north of Chengdu. The Shu officials formed ranks below the bridge. Yan came in a traveling carriage, dressed in white on a white horse, leading a sheep, with a grass rope about his neck, bound face-forward and holding a jade disk, with a coffin borne behind.

sentences.zh: 魏王下馬受其璧，崇韜釋其縛，及燔其櫬，衍率偽百官東北舞蹈謝恩。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei dismounted to receive his jade disk; Chongtao released his bonds and burned his coffin; Yan led the usurper officials in dancing toward the northeast to give thanks for imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wei dismounted to receive the jade disk. Guo Chongtao released his bonds and burned the coffin. Yan led the Shu officials in the ritual dance toward the northeast to thank the throne for its grace.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，拜，魏王、崇韜、李嚴皆答拜。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished they bowed; the Prince of Wei, Chongtao, and Li Yan all returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished they bowed, and the Prince of Wei, Guo Chongtao, and Li Yan all returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 二十八日，王師入成都。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day the imperial army entered Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth the imperial army entered Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 自起師至入蜀城，凡七十五日。

translations.literal: From the raising of the army to entry into the Shu capital, seventy-five days in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the raising of the army to entry into the Shu capital, seventy-five days in all.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：以下原本殘闕。

translations.literal: (Note: Below this the original text is defective and incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: Below this point the original text is defective and incomplete.

sentences.zh: 據《歐陽史》云：同光四年，衍行至秦川驛，莊宗用伶人景進計，遣宦者向延嗣誅其族。

translations.literal: According to the 《History of Ouyang》: In the fourth year of Tongguang, as Yan traveled to Qinchuan Post, Zhuangzong followed the actor Jing Jin's counsel and sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to execute his clan.
translations.idiomatic: According to Ouyang's History: In Tongguang year 4, as Yan traveled to Qinchuan Post, Emperor Zhuangzong followed the actor Jing Jin's counsel and sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to execute his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，封衍順正公，以諸侯葬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shunzheng and buried with the rites due a feudal lord.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 2 he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shunzheng and buried with the rites due a feudal lord.

sentences.zh: 《五代史補》：王建在許下時，尤不逞，嘗坐事遭徒，但無杖痕爾。

translations.literal: The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 says: When Wang Jian was at Xuchang he was especially unruly; once for an offense he was sentenced to penal servitude, but bore no marks of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: The Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties records: When Wang Jian was at Xuchang he was especially unruly. Once he was sentenced to penal servitude for an offense, but bore no marks of beating.

sentences.zh: 及據蜀，得馬涓為從事，涓好詆訐，建恐為所譏，因問曰：「竊聞外議，以吾曾遭徒刑，有之乎！」

translations.literal: When he held Shu he obtained Ma Juan as an aide; Juan loved to slander and denounce, and Jian feared being mocked by him, so he asked, "I have heard in private that outsiders say I once suffered penal servitude—is it so!"
translations.idiomatic: Once he held Shu he took Ma Juan as an aide. Juan loved to slander others, and Wang Jian feared his mockery. He asked, "I hear outsiders say I once suffered penal servitude—is that true?

sentences.zh: 涓對曰：「有之。」

translations.literal: Juan replied, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: Juan answered, "It is true."

sentences.zh: 建恃無杖痕，且對眾，因袒背以示涓曰：「請足下試看，有遭杖責而肌肉如是耶！」

translations.literal: Jian relied on having no staff marks and, before the assembly, bared his back to show Juan, saying, "Please, sir, look—could one who suffered beating have flesh like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, confident he bore no beating marks, bared his back before the assembly and said to Juan, "Look, sir—could flesh look like this after a beating?"

sentences.zh: 涓知其詐，乃撫背而嘆曰：「大奇，當時何處得此好膏藥來。」

translations.literal: Juan knew it was a fraud; he stroked Jian's back and sighed, "Marvelous—where ever did you get such fine salve at the time!"
translations.idiomatic: Juan saw through the deception. He stroked Wang Jian's back and sighed, "Remarkable—where did you find such fine salve?"

sentences.zh: 賓佐皆失色，而涓晏然。

translations.literal: The guests and aides all changed color, but Juan remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The guests all blanched, but Juan remained perfectly calm.

sentences.zh: 王建之僭號也，惟翰林學士最承恩顧，侍臣或諫其禮過，建曰：「蓋汝輩未之見也。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian usurped the imperial title, only the Hanlin academicians received the greatest favor; attendant ministers sometimes remonstrated that his courtesies went too far, and Jian said, "You people simply have not seen how it was.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian declared himself emperor, Hanlin academicians received the greatest favor. Some courtiers said his courtesies went too far. Wang Jian replied, "You simply have not seen how it was done before.

sentences.zh: 且吾在神策軍時，主內門魚鑰，見唐朝諸帝待翰林學士，雖交友不若也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when I was in the Shence Army and held the inner gate's fish-shaped keys, I saw how Tang emperors treated Hanlin academicians—even close friends were not treated so well.
translations.idiomatic: When I was in the Shence Army and held the keys to the inner gate, I saw how Tang emperors treated Hanlin academicians—even their closest friends were not honored so richly.

sentences.zh: 今我恩顧，比當時才有百分之一爾，何謂之過當耶！」

translations.literal: My favor today is only one hundredth of what it was then—how can you call it excessive!"
translations.idiomatic: My favor today is only one hundredth of what it was then—how can you call that excessive?

sentences.zh: 論者多之。

translations.literal: Many commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Many commentators praised his reply.

sentences.zh: 杜光庭，長安人，應《九經》舉不第。

translations.literal: Du Guangting was a native of Chang'an; he entered the Nine Classics examination and did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guangting came from Chang'an. He took the Nine Classics examination and failed.

sentences.zh: 時長安有潘尊師者，道術甚高，僖宗所重，光庭素所希慕，數遊其門。

translations.literal: At the time in Chang'an there was Master Pan the Honored, whose Daoist arts were very lofty and whom Emperor Xizong esteemed; Guangting had long admired him and often visited his gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an there was Master Pan, a Daoist of great renown whom Emperor Xizong esteemed. Guangting had long admired him and often visited his house.

sentences.zh: 當僖宗之幸蜀也，觀蜀中道門牢落，思得名士以主張之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong went in person to Shu, he observed that the Daoist community in Shu was sparse and thought to obtain a famous scholar to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, he saw that the Daoist community there was in decline and wished to find a leading figure to revive it.

sentences.zh: 駕回，詔潘尊師使於兩街，求其可者，尊師奏曰：「臣觀兩街之眾，道聽途說，一時之俊即有之，至於掌教之士，恐未合應聖旨。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, an edict sent Master Pan as envoy to the Two Streets to seek a suitable man; the Master memorialized, saying, "Your servant observes that among the masses of the Two Streets there are those who repeat hearsay—men of momentary talent may be found, but as for one to direct teaching, I fear none will suit the holy edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, he sent Master Pan to search the Two Streets for a suitable candidate. Pan memorialized: "Among the Daoists of the Two Streets one may find men of passing talent who repeat hearsay, but as for one fit to lead teaching, I fear none will meet Your Majesty's intent.

sentences.zh: 臣於科場中識《九經》杜光庭，其人性簡而氣清，量寬而識遠，且困於風塵，思欲脫屣名利久矣，以臣愚思之，非光庭不可。」

translations.literal: Your servant knew Du Guangting of the Nine Classics examination in the examination field; his nature is simple and his spirit clear, his capacity broad and his insight far-reaching; moreover he is weary of the dust of the world and has long wished to shake off fame and profit—in your servant's foolish thought, none but Guangting will do."
translations.idiomatic: I know Du Guangting from the examination grounds—a man of simple nature and clear spirit, broad in capacity and far in insight, weary of the world's turmoil and long eager to cast off fame and profit. In my humble judgment, none but Guangting will do.

sentences.zh: 僖宗詔而問之，一見大悅，遂令披戴，仍賜紫衣，號曰廣成先生，即日馳驛遣之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong summoned and questioned him; at first sight he was greatly pleased, ordered him invested and robed, further bestowed purple garments, styled him Master of Broad Completion, and that same day sent him post-haste by relay.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong summoned Guangting and was delighted at first sight. He had him invested as a Daoist priest, bestowed purple robes, styled him Master of Broad Completion, and sent him post-haste to Shu that same day.

sentences.zh: 及王建據蜀，待之愈厚，又號為天師。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian held Shu he treated him still more generously and again styled him Celestial Master.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian held Shu he treated Guangting even more generously and again styled him Celestial Master.

sentences.zh: 光庭嘗以《道》、《德》二經註者雖多，皆未能演暢其旨，因著《廣成義》八十卷，他術稱是，識者多之。）〉

translations.literal: Guangting once observed that although commentators on the Dao and De Classics were many, none had been able to unfold their meaning fully; he therefore composed the 《Broad Completion Exegesis》 in eighty chapters, and in other arts was likewise praised—men of insight approved him.")〉
translations.idiomatic: Guangting once observed that although many had commented on the Dao and De Classics, none had fully unfolded their meaning. He therefore composed the Broad Completion Exegesis in eighty chapters and was likewise praised in other arts—men of insight approved him.")〉

sentences.zh: 孟知祥，字保裔，邢州龍岡人也。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang, styled Baoyi, was a native of Longgang in Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang, styled Baoyi, came from Longgang in Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖察，父道，世為郡校。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Cha, his father Dao; for generations they were prefectural military officers.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Cha and his father Dao; for generations the family served as prefectural military officers.

sentences.zh: 伯父方立，終於邢洺節度使，從父遷，位至澤潞節度使。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Fangli ended as military governor of Xing-Ming; his father's younger brother Qian rose to military governor of Ze-Lu.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Fangli became military governor of Xing-Ming; his uncle Qian rose to military governor of Ze-Lu.

sentences.zh: 知祥在後唐莊宗同光三年，授西川節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang under Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong, Zhixiang was appointed deputy military governor of Xichuan with authority over military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Tang Tongguang year 3, Emperor Zhuangzong appointed Zhixiang deputy military governor of Xichuan with full authority over military affairs.

sentences.zh: 天成中，安重誨專權用事，以知祥莊宗舊識，方據大藩，慮久而難制，潛欲圖之。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era An Chonghui monopolized power; because Zhixiang was an old acquaintance of Zhuangzong and now held a great frontier post, he feared that in time he would be hard to control and secretly wished to scheme against him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng reign An Chonghui monopolized power. Because Zhixiang was an old acquaintance of Zhuangzong and now held a great frontier post, An feared he would grow ungovernable and secretly plotted against him.

sentences.zh: 是時，客省使李嚴以嘗使於蜀，洞知其利柄，因獻謀於重誨，請以己為西川監軍，庶效方略，以制知祥，朝廷可之。

translations.literal: At this time the guest-house envoy Li Yan, because he had once been envoy to Shu and thoroughly knew its leverage points, therefore offered counsel to Chonghui, asking to be made military supervisor of Xichuan himself so that he might apply stratagems to control Zhixiang; the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The guest-house envoy Li Yan, who had once served as envoy to Shu and knew its leverage points well, offered An Chonghui a plan: appoint him military supervisor of Xichuan so he could apply stratagems to control Zhixiang. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 及嚴至蜀，知祥延接甚至，徐謂嚴曰：「都監前因奉使，請兵伐蜀，遂使東、西兩川俱至破滅，川中之人，其怨已深。

translations.literal: When Yan reached Shu, Zhixiang received him with the utmost courtesy and slowly said to Yan, "Supervisor, on your former mission you requested troops to attack Shu, causing both eastern and western Chuan to be utterly destroyed—the people of the river valleys bear deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yan reached Shu, Zhixiang received him with the utmost courtesy and said slowly, "Supervisor, on your former mission you requested troops to attack Shu and brought ruin on both eastern and western Chuan. The people of the river valleys bear deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 今既復來，人情大駭，固奉為不暇也。」

translations.literal: Now that you have come again, popular feeling is greatly alarmed—I truly have no leisure to receive you."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have come again, the people are terrified. I truly have no leisure to receive you."

sentences.zh: 〈（案：此句疑有舛誤。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: This sentence is suspected of corruption.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Note: This sentence is suspected of textual corruption.)〉

sentences.zh: 即遣人拽下階，斬於階前。

translations.literal: He immediately sent men to drag him down the steps and behead him before the steps.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately had men drag Yan down the steps and behead him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》云：李嚴至境上，遣人持書候知祥，知祥盛兵見之，冀嚴懼而不來，嚴聞之自若。

translations.literal: (The 《History of Ouyang》 says: When Li Yan reached the border he sent a man with a letter to greet Zhixiang; Zhixiang displayed his army in strength, hoping Yan would be afraid and not come; Yan heard of this and remained composed.
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang's History records: When Li Yan reached the border he sent a letter ahead to Zhixiang. Zhixiang displayed his army in strength, hoping Yan would be afraid and turn back. Yan heard of this and remained perfectly composed.

sentences.zh: 天成二年正月，嚴至成都，知祥置酒召嚴，因責嚴曰：「今諸方鎮已罷監軍，公何得來？」

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tiancheng Yan reached Chengdu; Zhixiang set out wine and summoned Yan, then reproached him, saying, "Now the various frontier posts have all abolished military supervisors—how dare you come?"
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tiancheng year 2 Li Yan reached Chengdu. Zhixiang set out wine and summoned him, then rebuked him: "Every other frontier post has abolished military supervisors—how dare you come?

sentences.zh: 《鑒戒錄》云：李嚴於天成初復來臨護，孟祖加之禮分，從容數其五罪，命劍斬之。

translations.literal: The 《Record of Mirrors and Warnings》 says: Li Yan came again in the early Tiancheng era to serve as supervisor; the Meng founder treated him with courtesy, calmly enumerated his five crimes, and ordered him cut down with the sword.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Mirrors and Warnings records: Li Yan returned early in the Tiancheng era as military supervisor. Meng Zhixiang treated him courteously, calmly enumerated five crimes, and ordered him executed by the sword.

sentences.zh: 與《薛史》異。）〉

translations.literal: This differs from the 《History of Xue》.")〉
translations.idiomatic: This differs from Xue Juzheng's History.")〉

sentences.zh: 其後朝廷每除劍南牧守，皆令提兵而往，或千或百，分守郡城。

translations.literal: Thereafter whenever the court appointed a prefect or shepherd of Jiannan, it ordered him to lead troops thither—a thousand or a hundred—and garrison the prefectural cities in division.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter whenever the court appointed a Jiannan prefect or governor, it ordered him to bring troops—a thousand or a hundred—and garrison the prefectural cities.

sentences.zh: 時董璋作鎮東川已數年矣，亦有雄據之意。

translations.literal: At the time Dong Zhang had held Dongchuan for several years and likewise cherished the ambition to dominate by force.
translations.idiomatic: By then Dong Zhang had held Dongchuan for several years and likewise harbored ambitions of domination.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷以夏魯奇鎮遂州，李仁矩鎮閬州，皆領兵數千人赴鎮，復授以密旨，令制禦兩川。

translations.literal: It happened that the court stationed Xia Luqi at Sui Prefecture and Li Renju at Lang Prefecture, each leading several thousand troops to their posts, and further gave them secret instructions to control and restrain the Two Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: The court stationed Xia Luqi at Suizhou and Li Renju at Langzhou, each leading several thousand troops, and gave them secret orders to control both Chuan regions.

sentences.zh: 董璋覺之，乃與知祥通好，結為婚家，以固輔車之勢。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang perceived this and thereupon established friendly relations with Zhixiang, becoming affines by marriage to strengthen their mutual-support alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang perceived the threat and made peace with Zhixiang, sealing the bond with a marriage alliance to strengthen their mutual support.

sentences.zh: 知祥慮唐軍驟至，與遂、閬兵合，則勢不可支吾，遂與璋協謀，令璋以本部軍先取閬州，知祥遣大將軍李仁罕、趙廷隱率軍圍遂州。

translations.literal: Zhixiang feared that if Tang troops suddenly arrived and joined with the forces of Sui and Lang he could not hold out; he therefore plotted with Zhang, ordering Zhang to take Lang Prefecture first with his own division while Zhixiang sent the great generals Li Renhan and Zhao Tingyin to lead troops in besieging Sui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang feared that if Tang troops arrived suddenly and joined forces from Suizhou and Langzhou he could not hold out. He plotted with Zhang: Zhang would seize Langzhou first with his own troops while Zhixiang sent Generals Li Renhan and Zhao Tingyin to besiege Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 長興元年冬，唐軍伐蜀，至劍門。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Changxing the Tang army attacked Shu and reached Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Changxing year 1 the Tang army attacked Shu and reached Jianmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 二年，以遂、閬既陷，又糧運不接，乃班師。

translations.literal: In the second year, because Sui and Lang had already fallen and moreover supply transports did not link up, they withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, with Suizhou and Langzhou already fallen and supplies cut off, the Tang army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三年，知祥又破董璋，乃自領東、西兩川節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year Zhixiang again defeated Dong Zhang and thereupon personally assumed the post of military governor of both eastern and western Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zhixiang defeated Dong Zhang and assumed command of both eastern and western Chuan himself.

sentences.zh: 應順元年，以劍南東兩川節度使、王稱我帝於蜀，改元明德。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yingshun, as military governor of the eastern and western Two Chuan of Jiannan, he styled himself emperor in Shu and changed the era name to Mingde.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yingshun, as military governor of both Chuan regions, he declared himself emperor in Shu and adopted the era name Mingde.

sentences.zh: 七月卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：《孟知祥傳》，《永樂大典》原闕，今采《冊府元龜》僭偽部以存梗概。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: The biography of Meng Zhixiang was originally missing in the 《Yongle Encyclopedia》; the present text draws on the usurpers section of the 《Imperial Archive of the State》 to preserve the outline.")〉
translations.idiomatic: (Note: Meng Zhixiang's biography was originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia; the present text draws on the usurpers section of the Imperial Archive of the State to preserve the outline.")〉

sentences.zh: 昶，知祥之第三子也。

translations.literal: Chang was Zhixiang's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was Meng Zhixiang's third son.

sentences.zh: 〈（《宋朝事實》云：昶，初名仁贊。

translations.literal: (The 《Facts of the Song Dynasty》 says: Chang's original name was Renzan.
translations.idiomatic: (The Facts of the Song Dynasty records that Chang's original name was Renzan.

sentences.zh: 《揮麈餘話》云：昶，字保元。）〉

translations.literal: The 《Remaining Tales Waving the Whisk》 says: Chang, styled Baoyuan.")〉
translations.idiomatic: The Remaining Tales Waving the Whisk gives his style as Baoyuan.")〉

sentences.zh: 母李氏，本莊宗之嬪御，以賜知祥。

translations.literal: His mother was the Lady Li, originally a concubine of Zhuangzong, given to Zhixiang as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Li had originally been a concubine of Emperor Zhuangzong, given to Meng Zhixiang as a gift.

sentences.zh: 唐天祐十六年，歲在己卯，十一月十四日，生昶於太原。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Tianyou in Tang, the year jimao, on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month, Chang was born at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang Tianyou year 16, on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month of the jimao year, Chang was born at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 及知祥鎮蜀，昶與其母從知祥妻瓊華長公主同入於蜀。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang took command of Shu, Chang and his mother entered Shu together with Zhixiang's wife, the Princess of Qionghua the Eldest.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Zhixiang took command of Shu, Chang and his mother entered Shu together with his wife, the Eldest Princess of Qionghua.

sentences.zh: 知祥僭號，偽冊為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang usurped the imperial title, he falsely enfeoffed him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Zhixiang declared himself emperor, he named Chang crown prince.

sentences.zh: 知祥卒，遂襲其偽位，時年十六，尚稱明德元年。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang died, he thereupon inherited the usurper's throne; he was sixteen years old, and the era was still called Mingde year 1.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Zhixiang died, Chang succeeded to the throne at sixteen, still in the first year of the Mingde era.

sentences.zh: 及偽明德四年冬，偽詔改明年為廣政元年，是歲即晉天福三年也。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of the usurper era Mingde, a usurper edict changed the next year to Guangzheng year 1—that year was the third year of Tianfu in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Mingde year 4 an edict renamed the coming year Guangzheng year 1—the same year as Jin Tianfu year 3.

sentences.zh: 偽廣政十三年，偽上尊號為睿文英武仁聖明孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of the usurper era Guangzheng, the usurper court bestowed the honorific title Emperor Sagacious in Culture, Heroic in Arms, Benevolent and Sage, Bright and Filial.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangzheng year 13 the court bestowed on him the honorific title Emperor Sagacious in Culture, Heroic in Arms, Benevolent and Sage, Bright and Filial.

sentences.zh: 皇朝乾德三年春，王師平蜀，詔昶舉族赴闕，賜甲第於京師，迨其臣下賜賫甚厚，尋冊封楚王。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Qiande of Our Dynasty, the imperial army pacified Shu; an edict ordered Chang and his entire clan to come to court; a fine mansion in the capital was bestowed; his ministers and subordinates received lavish gifts; soon he was enfeoffed as King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Our Dynasty's Qiande year 3 the imperial army pacified Shu. An edict summoned Chang and his entire clan to court, granted them a fine mansion in the capital, richly rewarded his ministers, and soon enfeoffed him as King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 是歲秋，卒於東京，時年四十七，事具皇家日曆。

translations.literal: That autumn he died in the Eastern Capital, aged forty-seven; the affair is fully recorded in the imperial calendar.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he died in the Eastern Capital at the age of forty-seven; the full account appears in the imperial calendar.

sentences.zh: 自知祥同光二年丙戌歲入蜀，父子相繼，凡四十年而亡。

translations.literal: From Zhixiang's entry into Shu in the bingxu year, the second year of Tongguang, father and son succeeded one another—for forty years in all before perishing.
translations.idiomatic: From Meng Zhixiang's entry into Shu in Tongguang year 2, father and son ruled in succession for forty years before the state fell.

sentences.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：孟知祥之入蜀，視其險固，陰有割據之志。

translations.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: When Meng Zhixiang entered Shu he observed its rugged defensibility and secretly cherished the ambition to carve out a domain.
translations.idiomatic: (The Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties records: When Meng Zhixiang entered Shu he saw how rugged and defensible it was and secretly resolved to carve out his own domain.

sentences.zh: 洎抵成都，值晚，且憩於郊外。

translations.literal: When he reached Chengdu it was already evening, and he rested for a while in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Chengdu it was already evening, and he rested in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 有推小車子過者，其物皆以袋盛，知祥見，問曰：「汝車所勝幾袋？」

translations.literal: A man pushing a small cart passed by; his goods were all packed in bags. Zhixiang saw this and asked, "How many bags can your cart bear?"
translations.idiomatic: A man pushing a small cart passed by, his goods packed in bags. Zhixiang asked, "How many bags can your cart hold?

sentences.zh: 推者曰：「極力不過兩袋。」

translations.literal: The pusher said, "With full effort, no more than two bags."
translations.idiomatic: The man answered, "At most two bags, with all my strength."

sentences.zh: 知祥惡之，後果兩代而亡。

translations.literal: Zhixiang took this as ill-omened; in the end, after two generations, the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang took this as a bad omen—and indeed, two generations later the state fell.

sentences.zh: 知祥與董璋有隙，舉兵討之。

translations.literal: Zhixiang had a rift with Dong Zhang and raised troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang fell out with Dong Zhang and raised an army against him.

sentences.zh: 璋素勇悍，聞知祥之來也，以為送死。

translations.literal: Zhang had always been fierce and bold; hearing that Zhixiang was coming, he thought it was delivering himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang had always been fierce and bold. When he heard Meng Zhixiang was coming, he thought Zhixiang was marching to his death.

sentences.zh: 諸將兩端，李鎬為知祥判官，深憂之。

translations.literal: The generals wavered between two sides; Li Gao served as Zhixiang's aide and was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wavered. Li Gao, Meng Zhixiang's aide, was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 及將戰，知祥欲示閑暇，自寫一書以遺董璋。

translations.literal: When battle was about to be joined, Zhixiang wished to show leisure and personally wrote a letter to send to Dong Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle Meng Zhixiang wished to appear at ease and personally wrote a letter to Dong Zhang.

sentences.zh: 無何，舉筆輒誤書「董」為「重」字，不悅久之。

translations.literal: Before long, each time he raised the brush he mistakenly wrote the character for Dong as the character for heavy, and was displeased for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he kept mistakenly writing the character for Dong as the character for heavy, and was displeased for a long while.

sentences.zh: 鎬在側大喜，且引諸將賀於馬前，知祥不測，曰：「事未可測，何賀耶！」

translations.literal: Gao at his side was greatly pleased and led the generals in congratulation before his horse; Zhixiang could not fathom it and said, "The affair is not yet knowable—why congratulate!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao beside him was delighted and led the generals in congratulation before his horse. Meng Zhixiang could not understand and said, "The outcome is not yet known—why congratulate!

sentences.zh: 鎬曰：「其『董』字『艹』下施『重』。

translations.literal: Gao said, "The character for Dong has the grass radical above with heavy placed beneath.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao said, "The character for Dong has the grass radical on top with heavy beneath it.

sentences.zh: 今大王去『艹』書『重』是『董』已無頭，此必勝之兆也。」

translations.literal: Now Your Highness has removed the grass and written heavy—this means Dong has lost his head; it is surely an omen of victory."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has removed the grass and written heavy—Dong has lost his head. This is surely an omen of victory.

sentences.zh: 於是三軍欣然，一戰而董璋敗。）〉

translations.literal: Thereupon the three armies were joyful; in a single battle Dong Zhang was defeated.")〉
translations.idiomatic: The three armies took heart, and in a single battle Dong Zhang was defeated.")〉

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔張孟陽為《劍閣銘》云：「惟蜀之門，作固作鎮，世濁則逆，道清斯順。」

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In former times Zhang Mengyang composed the 《Inscription on Jiange》, saying, "Only the gate of Shu—made firm, made a barrier; when the age is turbid then rebellion, when the Way is clear then submission."
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Long ago Zhang Mengyang composed the Inscription on Jiange Pass: "Shu is the gate of the realm—made firm, made a barrier. When the age is corrupt men rebel; when the Way is clear they submit.

sentences.zh: 是知自古坤維之地，遇亂代則閉之而不通，逢興運則取之如俯拾。

translations.literal: From this one knows that from antiquity the land of the southwest corner, meeting a chaotic age, is shut and not passed through; meeting a flourishing fortune, is taken as if picking up from the ground.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that since antiquity the southwest has been closed off in ages of chaos and taken as easily as picking something from the ground when fortune smiles.

sentences.zh: 然唐氏之入蜀也，兵力雖勝，帝道猶昏，故數年間得之復失。

translations.literal: Yet when the house of Tang entered Shu, although military strength prevailed, the imperial Way was still dim, and therefore within a few years what was gained was again lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Tang entered Shu, though their armies prevailed, the imperial Way was still clouded, and within a few years what they gained they lost again.

sentences.zh: 及皇上之平蜀也，煦之以堯日，和之以舜風，故比戶之民，悅而從化。

translations.literal: When Our Emperor pacified Shu, he warmed it with the sun of Yao and harmonized it with the wind of Shun; therefore household after household of the people gladly submitted to transformation.
translations.idiomatic: When Our Emperor pacified Shu, he warmed it with the sun of Yao and harmonized it with the wind of Shun, so that household after household gladly submitted.

sentences.zh: 且夫王衍之遭季世也，則赤族於秦川；

translations.literal: Moreover, Wang Yan, meeting a degenerate age, had his entire clan exterminated in the Qin river region;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, meeting a degenerate age, had his entire clan exterminated in the Qin river region;

sentences.zh: 孟昶之遇明代也，則受封於楚甸。

translations.literal: Meng Chang, meeting a bright age, received enfeoffment in the Chu domains.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang, meeting a bright age, was enfeoffed in the Chu domains.

sentences.zh: 雖俱為亡國之主，何幸與不幸相去之遠也！

translations.literal: Although both were lords of perished states, how far apart are fortune and misfortune!
translations.idiomatic: Although both were rulers of fallen states, how vast is the distance between fortune and misfortune!
